balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For ZhongAn Online P & C Insurance Co., Ltd.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For ZhongAn Online P & C Insurance Co., Ltd.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For ZhongAn Online P & C Insurance Co., Ltd.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For ZhongAn Online P & C Insurance Co., Ltd.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For ZhongAn Online P & C Insurance Co., Ltd.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For ZhongAn Online P & C Insurance Co., Ltd.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For ZhongAn Online P & C Insurance Co., Ltd.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom. Net income in FY2025 and the 2025 capital raise include several non-recurring items worth separating from the run rate: a gain on disposal of ZA International (the Hong Kong/overseas JV), an impairment on a different joint-venture stake, proceeds from a new equity issuance (placement), and a repurchase-agreement financing line on the balance sheet. None of these are underwriting or investment income.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)
  • Adjusted net income attributable (which strips the ZA International gain and JV impairment) versus reported net income

premiums.title: Gross written premiums & net earned premium
premiums.content:
Gross written premiums (GWP) is the total premium ZhongAn wrote in the period before reinsurance and before it is recognised as revenue. Net earned premium was the HKFRS 4 revenue-recognition figure (premium earned net of reinsurance) used before the 2023 switch to HKFRS 17.

For ZhongAn Online P & C Insurance Co., Ltd.: GWP is the cleanest read on new business volume. FY2025 GWP grew +6.9% to RMB 35,735m, but H1 2026 GWP was -0.6% because the consumer-finance guarantee insurance line (sold alongside online lending) is being run off deliberately: consumer-finance GWP fell ~79% while every other line grew +14.6%. The reported HKFRS 17 insurance revenue lags GWP, so revenue growth (+12.9% in H1 2026) currently looks stronger than underlying new business.

What to watch:

  • GWP ex-consumer-finance as the real growth signal while the run-off continues
  • The widening gap between GWP and HKFRS 17 revenue as a timing, not a quality, issue

cor.title: Combined operating ratio
cor.content:
The combined operating ratio (COR) is (claims incurred + operating expenses) / net earned premium. Below 100% means the underwriting book is profitable before investment income; above 100% means premiums alone do not cover claims and costs.

For ZhongAn Online P & C Insurance Co., Ltd.: COR has been consistently above 95% (95.2% FY2023, 96.9% FY2024, 95.8% FY2025), meaning underwriting profit is thin and most of net income depends on net investment income and scale. A rising COR while GWP growth slows is the combination to watch.

What to watch:

  • COR trending toward or above 100%
  • Whether COR improvement is coming from the loss ratio (claims experience) or the expense ratio (cost discipline) — the two are not disclosed separately in the CSV

solvencyInvestment.title: Solvency ratio & net investment income
solvencyInvestment.content:
The comprehensive solvency ratio is regulatory capital over required capital under China's C-ROSS regime; insurers are typically required to stay above 100%, with 150%+ considered comfortable. Net investment income is the return earned on the investment portfolio backing premiums and capital.

For ZhongAn Online P & C Insurance Co., Ltd.: the solvency ratio has drifted down from 472% (FY2021) to 227-242% (FY2024-25) as the balance sheet has grown and capital has been returned/absorbed, but remains well above the regulatory floor — the 2025 equity placement rebuilt some of this buffer. Net investment income is volatile with China's bond and equity markets and, given thin underwriting margins (see COR), is a swing factor in net income.

What to watch:

  • Solvency ratio approaching regulatory minimums, which would force capital raises or business restraint
  • Net investment income volatility swamping underwriting profit in a weak markets year

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For ZhongAn Online P & C Insurance Co., Ltd.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For ZhongAn Online P & C Insurance Co., Ltd.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
